metaDescription: We compared six VEVOR 6L ultrasonic cleaners on heater range, ultrasonic power, degassing and controls to help you pick the right workshop-size tank.
introParagraphs: A 6 L ultrasonic cleaner is the workshop-size step up from the little jewelry tubs, and it is the capacity most hobbyists, repair benches and small shops settle on. The tank is big enough for a carburetor, a tray of watch parts, a handful of nozzles or several pairs of glasses at once, yet it still sits on a bench and plugs into a normal outlet. That balance is why so many buyers search for it by size alone.

Every listing in this lineup is a VEVOR 6L model running at 40 kHz, so the real differences are subtler than the box suggests: ultrasonic power from 120W to 180W, heater range from 80°C to 110°C, a degassing mode on some units, and a digital panel versus a knob. We evaluated six models based on product specs and buyer feedback, and we dropped the vinyl record versions and a near-duplicate listing to keep the comparison honest.
Use the picks below as a starting point, then work through the buying criteria and decision tables to match the controls and heating to the jobs you actually run.

products.name: VEVOR 6L 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, 180W with Heater
products.description:
This is the plain, well-specified core model of the group. A 6 L 304 stainless tank measuring 12.8 by 6.9 by 5.9 inches is driven by three 60W transducers for 180W of ultrasonic power at 40 kHz, and a 200W heater covers 0 to 80°C (176°F). A digital display sets both time, from 0 to 30 minutes, and temperature, and the listing cites FCC, CE, RoHS and UL certification.

It does not add gimmicks, which is the point. There is no degassing mode and no special gentle setting, so you control the result with time, temperature and detergent. That suits jewelry, eyeglasses, watches, circuit boards, dental equipment and tableware, but 40 kHz is harsh on soft stones and delicate finishes, so it is a tool for hardy items.

In daily use you fill with warm water and a neutral cleaner, set the digital panel and walk away. Expect a heavy full tank and a spot to drain it. At 180W it matches the other 180W picks, but it has a lower heater rating than the 400W upgraded model and a narrower range than the 0 to 110°C unit, so it wins on balance rather than any single number.
products.bestFor: Most buyers who want a dependable 6 L cleaner with clear digital time and temperature settings.
pros: Three 60W transducers give 180W of ultrasonic power at 40 kHz
The 200W heater reaches 80°C to loosen grease and oily films
Digital panel sets time to 30 minutes and temperature precisely
Listing cites FCC, CE, RoHS and UL certification for peace of mind
cons: No degassing mode, so first minutes run less efficiently on fresh water
The 40 kHz output is too harsh for soft stones and fragile finishes
A full 6 L tank is heavy, and you need a spot nearby to drain it

products.name: VEVOR 6L 180W Ultrasonic Cleaner, Gentle Mode and Degassing
products.description:
The standout here is the pairing of a gentle mode with an upgraded degassing mode. Degassing pulls dissolved air out of fresh liquid, and the listing says the dual-power mode improves efficiency by 30 percent and helps reach holes and crevices. Alongside it you get 180W at 40 kHz, a 0 to 80°C heater and a 304 stainless tank with a scratch-protecting basket.

The gentle setting is useful because 40 kHz at full power can be rough on delicate parts, and a lower-power option lets you step down without buying a second machine. The tradeoff is more settings to learn, and the listing does not give a heater wattage or tank dimensions, so you are relying on the 6 L headline. Treat the efficiency figure as a manufacturer claim.

Ownership is easy, with a portable handle and a drainage system to empty the tank without lifting it. Next to the base 180W model, the extra modes are the main upgrade. The knob-operated VEVOR 6L unit with basket also offers degassing and dual power, so the choice comes down to a digital panel here versus a simple knob there.
products.bestFor: Buyers who clean both tough parts and more delicate items and want a lower-power option.
pros: Dual-power mode lets you step down from full 180W for delicate items
Upgraded degassing is claimed to lift efficiency by 30 percent
Built-in drainage and a portable handle simplify emptying the tank
The scratch-protecting basket keeps small parts off the steel floor
cons: Listing gives no heater wattage or exact tank dimensions to compare
More modes mean a longer learning curve than a plain timer and dial
The 30 percent efficiency gain is a maker claim, not a measured result

products.name: VEVOR 6L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control and Basket

specList.label: Control
specList.value: Knobs for frequency, time and temperature

products.description:
This model swaps menus for a knob. You adjust frequency, time and temperature by turning dials, and a digital display shows the values. Behind that sits a 304 stainless tank, a scratch-proof basket, an upgraded handle and the same dual power and degassing modes you find on the other upgraded unit, with the listing again claiming a 30 percent efficiency gain from degassing.

The knob is the real appeal for anyone who dislikes tapping small buttons, because a dial is easy to read and to grip with larger or less nimble fingers. It targets carburetor channels, spray nozzles and small parts, and the maker recommends a neutral detergent and warm water. The listing does not state ultrasonic wattage or heater power, so you cannot rank its output against the 180W models.

The cleaning ball and basket suspension help you hang parts evenly in the tank. Compared with the gentle-mode VEVOR 6L unit, which also has a gentle mode and degassing, this one trades a touch of display polish for easier dial control. At the mid point of the group on features, it fits people who want simple, tactile operation.
products.bestFor: People who prefer turning knobs to pressing buttons and want degassing for parts work.
pros: Large knobs set time and temperature without small menus or buttons
Dual power and degassing modes are rare in this lineup of 6 L tanks
The included basket and cleaning ball help suspend parts evenly
An upgraded handle makes carrying a full tank safer than a plain rim
cons: The listing gives no ultrasonic wattage or heater rating to compare
Knob steps are less exact than typing a figure on a digital keypad
At 40 kHz it still needs care with fragile jewelry and soft stones

products.name: VEVOR 6L Upgraded Ultrasonic Cleaner, 400W Heater
products.description:
The 400W heater is the headline, double what the base model carries. It pairs with 180W of ultrasonic power from two built-in transducers at 40 kHz, a 0 to 80°C range and a 0 to 30 minute timer, all in a 304 stainless tank with no leak seams. The listing also describes low-noise running, anti-slide rubber feet and heat dissipation.

A stronger heater brings the water to temperature sooner, which matters when you are cleaning grease, wax or oil from holes and crevices. The drain valve with a 1 m pipe is a genuine convenience, because emptying 6 L without lifting the tank is the least pleasant part of ownership. The tradeoff is that the maximum is still 80°C, so the extra wattage buys speed rather than a hotter bath.

Certified to CE, FCC and RoHS per the listing, it is aimed at jewelry, glasses, dentures, coins and shop use alike. Against the 200W base model it heats noticeably faster, while the 0 to 110°C unit goes hotter at the top end. Pick it when you run frequent greasy batches and want less waiting.
products.bestFor: Frequent greasy-parts cleaners who want faster warm-up and an easy drain.
pros: A 400W heater warms the bath faster than the 200W base model
The drain valve with a 1 m pipe empties the tank without lifting it
Anti-slide rubber feet and heat dissipation add stable, cooler running
Two transducers still deliver 180W of ultrasonic power at 40 kHz
cons: The ceiling is still 80°C, so extra wattage buys speed, not more heat
Only two transducers, so cavitation is spread less evenly in the tank
No degassing or gentle mode to step the power down for delicate items

products.name: VEVOR 6L Ultrasonic Cleaner, 0 to 110°C Heater
products.description:
This is the pick for the highest heat setting in the group. The listing gives a controllable cleaning temperature from 0 to 110°C, against 80°C on most siblings, together with 180W of ultrasonic power at 40 kHz. The tank and basket are 304 stainless steel, and the basket prevents scratches as items vibrate.

The extra range is for heavy grease on industrial components, where warmer liquid dissolves dirt faster. It also means more responsibility, since glued parts, plastics and many stones should never see that kind of heat, and the listing marketing around jewelry should not tempt you to run it hot. The listing does not give a heater wattage, so we cannot say how fast it gets there.

A portable handle and drainage make routine use manageable. Compared with the 400W unit capped at 80°C, this one reaches a higher temperature but may take longer to arrive. It is a specialist choice for mechanics, lab users and hobbyists with oily metal parts, and a plain 80°C model is enough for everyone else.
products.bestFor: Mechanics and hobbyists with heavy grease on metal parts who want a higher heat ceiling.
pros: Reaches 110°C, the highest heat setting among the 6 L picks here
Delivers 180W of ultrasonic output at 40 kHz like the base model
304 stainless tank and basket resist rust and protect parts from scratches
A handle and drainage system make emptying the 6 L tank easier
cons: Listing gives no heater wattage, so warm-up speed is unclear
High heat can damage glue, plastic and many gemstones if misused
No degassing or gentle mode to protect delicate items from full power

products.name: VEVOR 6L Ultrasonic Cleaner, 120W with Digital Display
products.description:
At 120W this is the least powerful of the group, a third below the 180W models. It still runs at 40 kHz and generates the same family of microbubbles the maker describes for carburetor channels, airbrush tips, watch bands and lab components, with a 0 to 80°C range and digital time and temperature settings. The stainless tank and basket are corrosion resistant, and an upgraded handle makes moving a full tank easier.

Lower power is not automatically worse. A gentler output spreads less energy through the tank, which can be kinder to thin or finished parts, and it generally means a less demanding machine. The cost is slower work on baked-on grease or stubborn deposits, and you should expect to run more cycles on heavy soil.

Setup is the same as its siblings, fill with warm water and a neutral cleaner, set the panel and start. It lacks the degassing and gentle modes found on the gentle-mode and knob-control units, so power is fixed. Compared with the 180W base model it trades some cleaning strength for a lower overall specification, which makes sense if your loads are light.
products.bestFor: Light-duty users cleaning small hardware, glasses and lightly soiled parts at lower power.
pros: At 120W it applies less energy, which suits lighter or thinner parts
Digital display sets time and temperature up to 80°C clearly
Corrosion-resistant stainless tank and basket protect items from scratches
An upgraded handle makes carrying a full tank easier than a plain rim
cons: Slower on baked-on grease than the 180W models in the same size tank
No degassing or gentle mode, so the output power is fixed at 120W
The listing gives no heater wattage to judge how fast it warms up

buyingCriteria.explanation: Ultrasonic watts decide how hard the cavitation hits, and a 6 L tank needs enough of it to fill the whole volume. Below about 100W a tank this size cleans noticeably slowly, while 150W to 200W is the usual range for general workshop use. The VEVOR 6L 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, 180W with Heater delivers 180W from three 60W transducers, while the VEVOR 6L Ultrasonic Cleaner, 120W with Digital Display runs at 120W. Choose 180W if you have greasy parts, and 120W only for light, regular rinses.

Warm liquid loosens grease and wax, so a heater shortens cycles, but wattage and temperature ceiling are two different things. Wattage sets how fast the bath warms up, and the ceiling sets how hot it can go. The VEVOR 6L Upgraded Ultrasonic Cleaner, 400W Heater has a 400W element but stops at 80°C, whereas the VEVOR 6L Ultrasonic Cleaner, 0 to 110°C Heater reaches 110°C. For most jobs 60°C to 80°C is plenty, and anything hotter should be reserved for hardy metal parts.

Fresh liquid holds dissolved air that absorbs cavitation energy, so a degassing mode runs a few minutes to purge it before real cleaning. It is a useful feature for 6 L tanks, where a lot of fresh water goes in at once. The VEVOR 6L 180W Ultrasonic Cleaner, Gentle Mode and Degassing and the VEVOR 6L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control both include it, and both cite a 30 percent efficiency gain. If you do not have it, run a plain 5 to 10 minute warm-up cycle with no parts in the tank.

How you set time and temperature changes the daily experience more than a spec sheet suggests. A digital panel lets you type exact values, while a knob is faster to read and easier to grip. The VEVOR 6L 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, 180W with Heater and the 120W model use digital panels, and the VEVOR 6L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control uses dials. Choose a knob if small buttons annoy you, and a digital panel if you repeat precise recipes.

A 6 L tank of water weighs about 6 kg before the stainless body and heater are counted, so lifting it to empty is awkward and sometimes unsafe. A drain valve or handle turns a chore into a quick job. The VEVOR 6L Upgraded Ultrasonic Cleaner, 400W Heater adds a valve and a 1 m pipe, and the VEVOR 6L 180W Ultrasonic Cleaner, Gentle Mode and Degassing lists drainage and a portable handle. Place the machine near a sink or bucket, and empty it only after it has cooled.

At 40 kHz every machine here is on the aggressive side, so item compatibility matters more than any spec. Soft stones such as pearls and opals, glued items, plated finishes and watches that are not water resistant should stay out. Every pick uses a 304 stainless tank, but only the VEVOR 6L 180W Ultrasonic Cleaner, Gentle Mode and Degassing offers a gentle mode, and the VEVOR 6L Ultrasonic Cleaner, 0 to 110°C Heater needs the most care because of its heat ceiling. If you clean mixed items, use a basket and never place parts directly on the tank floor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ultrasonic power and transducers
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated ultrasonic watts, transducer count and frequency across the lineup. The VEVOR 6L 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, 180W with Heater and the two upgraded units lead at 180W, while the 120W model sits at the bottom. All figures are manufacturer claims, so we used them to rank relative strength rather than as absolute cleaning performance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heating performance
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at heater wattage, temperature ceiling and range. The VEVOR 6L Upgraded Ultrasonic Cleaner, 400W Heater leads on wattage, the 0 to 110°C unit leads on ceiling, and the others cap at 80°C. Where a listing did not state a heater rating, we noted the gap rather than guess.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and modes
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared digital panels, knobs, degassing and gentle modes. The 180W gentle-mode unit and the knob-control unit are the only picks with degassing and dual power, so they scored higher on flexibility. Simpler digital-only models scored well on clarity and ease of use for repeat jobs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered drainage, handles, rubber feet and basket quality because a full 6 L tank is the main practical burden. The 400W unit with a 1 m drain pipe leads on emptying ease, and every model uses a 304 stainless tank and basket. We did not rank on price figures.

howWeEvaluated.title: Certification and value for a class
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted stated certifications, such as the FCC, CE, RoHS and UL cited for the 180W base model, and how much each model offers within the lineup. The base unit leads on balance, the 120W model on lower power, and the specialist heaters on temperature. We treated the 6 L, 40 kHz class as a fixed baseline for all six picks.

cards.label: Degassing and dual power
cards.text: Dissolved air in fresh liquid absorbs cavitation energy, so degassing purges it before the real clean, and dual power lets you drop output for delicate items. The VEVOR 6L 180W Ultrasonic Cleaner, Gentle Mode and Degassing and the VEVOR 6L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control both cite a 30 percent efficiency gain. Pick this side if you change water often or clean mixed items.

cards.label: Fixed power
cards.text: A fixed-power tank has fewer settings and is simpler to learn, but you manage air removal by running a short warm-up. The VEVOR 6L 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, 180W with Heater, the 400W unit, the 110°C unit and the 120W model fall here. Pick this side if you want a straightforward timer and temperature routine for similar parts.

faq.q: Which 6L ultrasonic cleaner is best for most buyers?
faq.a: The VEVOR 6L 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner, 180W with Heater is the safest all-round pick, with 180W, a 200W heater to 80°C and clear digital controls. If you clean varied items, the gentle-mode unit adds a lower power option. If you run greasy batches every day, the 400W heater unit warms faster.

faq.q: Is 6 L too big for jewelry and glasses?
faq.a: It is more tank than you need, but it works. A 6 L machine holds several pairs of glasses at once, and the 12.8 by 6.9 by 5.9 inch tank on the base model fits larger frames. The downside is storage, water volume and the 40 kHz output, which is harsher on fine jewelry. For rings alone, a smaller high-frequency tub is usually better.

faq.q: What does the degassing mode actually do?
faq.a: Fresh water holds dissolved air, which absorbs cavitation energy and cuts cleaning power. Degassing runs the transducers briefly to drive that air out before you add parts. The VEVOR 6L 180W Ultrasonic Cleaner, Gentle Mode and Degassing and the Knob Control unit both claim a 30 percent efficiency gain. Without degassing, run a warm-up cycle with no parts.

faq.q: Do I need a higher heat setting than 80°C?
faq.a: Rarely. Most jewelry, glasses and parts clean well between 40°C and 80°C, and heat above that can harm glue, plastic and many stones. The 0 to 110°C unit is meant for heavy industrial grease on hardy metal. If you are not sure, set a moderate temperature and run a longer cycle instead.

No, because more power is also harsher on delicate items. The 180W models clean tough soil faster than the 120W unit, but soft finishes, plating and thin parts can be damaged by full power. Match the wattage to the toughest thing you clean, and use a gentle or dual power mode where it is available.

faq.q: How do I look after a 6 L ultrasonic cleaner?
faq.a: Never run it empty, and always keep liquid above the minimum line. Let the tank cool before draining, and use the drain valve if you have one, as on the 400W model with its 1 m pipe. Wipe the stainless tank and basket dry, and keep the control panel away from splashes. Use only the cleaners the manual approves.

faq.q: Can I clean anything in a 6L ultrasonic cleaner?
faq.a: No. Pearls, opals, turquoise, emeralds, glued items and watches that are not water resistant should stay out. Treated stones and old worn prongs can also be shaken loose by vibration. Always hold items in a basket rather than placing them on the tank floor, and ask a professional if you are unsure.
